newsitem.title: USA: Wells Fargo president to retire.
newsitem.headline: Wells Fargo president to retire.

text.p: Wells Fargo & Co. said Wednesday its president, William Zuendt, aged 50, plans to retire later this year.

"I've always planned to retire early, but there were so many challenges and exciting developments throughout the 1990s that I kept postponing my decision," said Zuendt in a statement. "Now that we've acquired First Interstate and merged the two organisations, the timing seems right."
Effective immediately, four vice chairmen will form a team with Chairman Paul Hazen as part of a newly created Office of the Chairman, with three customer segments.
Vice Chairman Terri Dial, 47, will head the consumer and small business banking segment.
Vice Chairman Clyde Ostler, 50, will head investment groups, serving individual and institutional investors.
Vice Chairman Charlie Johnson, 55, will be responsible for wholesale banking, which serves commercial, corporate and real estate customers.
Vice Chairman and Chief Financial Officer Rod Jacobs will head finance, operations, systems and administrative groups that support the business units.

Zuendt joined Wells Fargo in 1973, with responsibility for its computer systems and operations. In 1980, he was elected an executive vice president and moved to the retail banking division, where he directed the bank's strategy throughout the decade. He became vice chairman in 1986, and president in January 1995.
Wells Fargo, based in San Francisco, acquired First Interstate Bancorp in April 1996.
Wells Fargo's stock fell $6.375 to $259.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
